newsitem.title: USA: Hilton attacks ITT sale of 5 hotels.
newsitem.headline: Hilton attacks ITT sale of 5 hotels.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp, in a sharply written letter to the board of directors of takeover target ITT Corp, on Monday attacked the terms of ITT's planned sale of five hotels to FelCor Suite Hotels Inc.
Part of the $200 million deal calls for ITT to receive a management fee for operating the hotels, but that provision would be severed if ITT underwent a change in control.

"We view these change of control provisions as irresponsible and unnecessary," Hilton Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach wrote. "In this regard, Hilton is willing to purchase the five hotels at the same price."

Bollenbach said Hilton was ready to acquire the five ITT Sheraton hotels, located throughout the United States, at the same price and on the same terms as FelCor, but Hilton would exclude the change of control provision.
"If ITT is looking to dispose of any more of its core assets, Hilton is a ready, willing and able buyer," he said.

ITT is the target of a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid by Hilton. The rival hotel and gambling company launched the offer in January. ITT rejected the bid, calling it inadequate, then it began shedding non-core assets and refocusing operations on its core hotels and gambling business.

ITT quickly defended the FelCor deal, saying FelCor requested the change-of-control provision. A spokesman said most of the recently announced management and franchise contracts between ITT and others contained the same provision.
In its letter, Hilton said its offer to acquire the five hotels was "clearly more advantageous to ITT shareholders."

But ITT lashed out at that contention. "The Felcor deal will be accretive to ITT earnings in 1998. Every asset sale that we have made since January 27, when Hilton launched their hostile offer, has been at exceptional prices and has added value for our shareholders," spokesman Jim Gallagher said.
ITT has sold its stake in French telecommunications company Alcatel Alstholm for about $830 million and agreed to sell its 50 percent stake in Madison Square Garden Inc for around $650 million.
The FelCor deal involved hotels that are significantly smaller than ITT Sheraton's major properties and are considered to be mostly in secondary markets for the company.

Financial analysts expect ITT, when it has completed its asset sales, will launch a buyback offer for a large number of its common shares or issue a lucrative one-time dividend to boost shareholder support as it defends against Hilton.

ITT owns and operates Sheraton brand hotels and Caesars resorts and casinos. Hilton operates Hilton Hotels in the United States and promotes Hilton overseas in a joint venture with Ladbroke Plc. It also owns Bally's brand and Hilton casinos.
